drafted_from: tool row in tools/fine-tune-a-small-model-on-a-persons-rules/tool-rows.json, do-work/train_an_adapter.py and test/test_fine_tune.py (model_runs_refuse_a_folder_that_is_not_a_decider); the refusal was run here, a real run needs torch and a decider model and is not run
start_here: Say to your AI: "Train an adapter on /work/out/train.jsonl with my decider model /work/models/decider-2b, my frame, rank 8, one epoch and a 30 minute budget, saved to /work/adapter." It writes a request file and runs train_an_adapter.py on your computer.
instructions: 1. Pour the two example rows into your own settings list (see pour), or make list:settings from them, then put your own seed, test share, set names and numbers in the build, train and score objects: every law, line, set name and number is yours, none is built in.

2. Build train.jsonl first with tool:build-training-rows-from-a-persons-rules. Ask the person for the time budget (a run can take most of an hour) and for the frame: the context each line is put in, holding {text}, exactly as their gate asks it.

3. The AI writes the request (base_model, frame, train_file, out, rank, epochs, lr, batch, budget_minutes, seed, lora_targets, optionally device, nice, threads) and runs python3 -I tools/fine-tune-a-small-model-on-a-persons-rules/do-work/train_an_adapter.py <request file>. The run uses low priority and few CPU threads, projects its total time after 20 steps and stops when the projection passes the budget.

4. Read the last line: {"result": {adapter, base, rank, alpha, targets, epochs, lr, batch, rows, minutes, final_loss, frame}} or {"error": ...}. Then measure it with tool:score-held-out-lines-with-a-small-model, with and without the adapter.

worked_examples.title: A folder that is not a decider model is refused before any training
worked_examples.ask: Train an adapter on my train.jsonl with the model folder /work/models.
worked_examples.given: From tools/fine-tune-a-small-model-on-a-persons-rules/test/test_fine_tune.py (test_model_runs_refuse_a_folder_that_is_not_a_decider), which I ran. Request: {"base_model": "/work/models", "frame": "{text}", "train_file": "/work/train.jsonl", "out": "/work/adapter", "rank": 8, "epochs": 1, "lr": 0.0001, "batch": 8, "budget_minutes": 1, "seed": 1, "lora_targets": ["q_proj"]} where /work/models is an empty folder and train.jsonl is empty. Command: python3 -I tools/fine-tune-a-small-model-on-a-persons-rules/do-work/train_an_adapter.py /work/request.json. It exits 2.
worked_examples.hands_back: {"error": "/work/models is not a decider model folder: it needs decider/ and decider_config.json"} Nothing is trained. With a real decider folder (decider-2b, for example) the run ends with {"result": {"adapter": ..., "minutes": ..., "final_loss": ...}} and train-info.json beside the adapter; a request with no out says "out is required: the folder the adapter is saved to".

lists.label: Settings
lists.holds: One row per tool and scope (a person, a film, a piece or the whole account): the settings that tool reads when it runs, as JSON. For the fine-tune tools the row id is record:setting:fine-tune-a-small-model-on-a-persons-rules~<scope_kind>~<scope_id> and its settings hold a build, a train and a score object that fill every request key the request leaves out.

Fine-tune settings for a second rule set

pour.how: Name the list you already keep for the same job and read it with records:read (its fields and row type). Run tool:pour-example-rows-into-my-list with that list as into and this kit list as kit_list: it matches each kit field to one of yours (your map, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), pours nothing under 80% and names the fields with no home, and otherwise answers the one records:write that adds the example rows beside your own.
